messages:
elaine: FYI customer reports spike in latency and a bunch of requests routing to EU despite them setting region=us-east in the SDK query param. They attached request examples and say the app sees ~250ms extra per request.
mark_support: can you paste one of the raw requests/headers from the customer? also which SDK + version?
elaine: SDK v2.3.1 (node). customer sent curl sample: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?region=us-east \
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" \
 -H \"X-Client-Region: us-east, eu-west\" \
 -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
They said our router logged the request to eu-west and they saw latency bump.
mark_support: thanks. quick check: router_bot logs for trace id?
router_bot: trace=tr_0a9c, route_evaluated=eu-west, route_reason=header_priority, headers={X-Client-Region: \"us-east, eu-west\"}, query.region=us-east
jorge_eng: interesting — router currently uses header precedence over query param. If header is multi-value we split on commas and pick the last token (historical quirk). That would explain eu-west selection.
tina_sre: confirmed in live logs for traces around that time: several requests have X-Client-Region=\"us-east, eu-west\" (note the space). The split logic doesn't trim whitespace and our comparator then picks last item.
qa_ash: repro on my laptop with node SDK v2.3.1: if you pass regions as array to headers axios joins to 'us-east, eu-west' automatically. Our SDK docs advise single-region string but devs sometimes pass arrays.
elaine: customer says they only set region in query param and never touched headers; they use an HTTP proxy in front of the app that injects geo tags — proxy sends both header and query param.
mark_support: immediate mitigation for customer: set explicit header X-Client-Region: us-east (single token) or remove the header at proxy level. Offer temporary credit for added latency while we fix. @anita_support can you handle credits communication?
anita_support: on it, will propose 25% for the affected window pending engineering fix.
jorge_eng: short-term router patch: change header parsing to split on commas, trim tokens, and prefer query param when present. Long-term: make precedence policy configurable per-tenant. I'll open a hotfix PR.
jorge_eng: repro steps I used: 
1) curl with query region=us-east and header X-Client-Region: \"us-east, eu-west\" 
2) observe router chooses eu-west
3) apply local change to parser: `parts = header.split(',').map(p => p.trim()).filter(Boolean); selected = parts[0]` 
4) confirm it picks us-east
qa_ash: can add unit + integration tests for multi-value header cases. I'll add a test to assert query param beats header when present.
tina_sre: I'll push a config change to edge to trim and canonicalize headers; low risk rollback plan ready.
dev_bot: deploy started for hotfix branch hotfix/header-canonicalize -> staging (CI passed) :rocket:
mark_support: ETA for prod patch?
jorge_eng: staging -> canary in prod in ~45m if no regressions, full rollout after 2h.
anita_support: I emailed customer with workaround and offered credit, they replied ok but asked for timeline — they want fix today.
mark_support: agreed prioritize. After patch we should update SDK docs and call out proxy behavior. Also add a note in troubleshooting KB: 'If you use proxies or middlewares that may append region headers, ensure header contains single token or use query param.'
elaine: added KB draft link: https://redwood.docs/internal/support/region-header-proxy.md
mark_support: closing loop items: 1) eng hotfix (jorge) 2) sre canary + rollout (tina) 3) QA tests (ash) 4) support comms + credit (anita) 5) docs + SDK patch (mark/jorge).
router_bot: deploy canary complete (nodes 3/3), monitoring shows normal QPS and no errors.
jorge_eng: canary passed, rolling out full patch now.
router_bot: rollout complete. impacted traces now routing to us-east when query param present.
elaine: customer confirmed after patch they see requests routed to us-east and latency back to normal. They accepted the credit. :thumbsup:
mark_support: great. we'll follow up with a minor SDK release that defensive-guards against passing arrays into region header. leaving thread open for postmortem notes.
qa_ash: I'll include test case IDs and link to PR in the postmortem.
elaine: thanks everyone!
